assets.identity_finding: Kraken publishes the asset as Dent on Ethereum (ERC-20) and describes a blockchain-based mobile operator and data exchange whose DENT token "powers the platform". Independently, the project's own DENTNet documentation publishes the DENT Token as "the core of the mobile data ecosystem" with a total supply of "100B" that "will not change", deposited into DENTNet "from ERC20 wallets" and, in the bridge guide, "from the Ethereum network" -- the same ticker, the same chain and the same telecommunications platform Kraken names. DISCLOSED LIMIT: no live official page publishes a contract address; dentwireless.com and dent-app.com now redirect to the successor brand Tunz (tunz.io, part of DT One), whose October 2025 notice states "Dent is now Tunz" and that "the DENT Token will continue to serve as a payment option within the app", the app site app.tunz.io still links www.dentnet.io as the project's blockchain, and the bridge UI at main.dentnet.io returns 404. This record is therefore a chain-level identity confirmed by two independent organisations and makes no exact-contract claim.

Kraken's own migration notice states that Gala Games (GALA) migrated contracts on 15 May 2023 and that "the official Ethereum contract address for GALA(v2) is 0xd1d2Eb1B1e90B638588728b4130137D262C87cae", consistent with Kraken's asset report publishing GALA on Ethereum (ERC-20). Independently, Gala's own Help Center article for adding $GALA to MetaMask on the Ethereum network publishes the identical contract address 0xd1d2Eb1B1e90B638588728b4130137D262C87cae. Two independent organisations therefore publish the same exact contract for the same ticker; GALA v1 is deprecated and no GalaChain native-coin claim is made.

Kraken publishes the asset as Meteora on Solana and describes a Solana-based liquidity infrastructure and DEX built on Dynamic Liquidity Market Maker technology. Independently, Meteora's own documentation publishes "MET SPL Address: METvsvVRapdj9cFLzq4Tr43xK4tAjQfwX76z3n6mWQL", a TGE date of 23 October 2025 and a fixed 1,000,000,000 MET supply, and its MET FAQ states the launch chain is Solana on the SPL token standard. The exact ticker MET is therefore bound by the project itself to one published Solana mint, distinct from the Solana native coin.

Kraken publishes the asset as River on BNB Chain and its asset page describes the chain-abstraction stablecoin system, the omni-CDP stablecoin satUSD and the PrimeVault and SmartVault products. Independently, River's own documentation publishes "RIVER Token Address" as 0xdA7AD9dea9397cffdDAE2F8a052B82f1484252B3 on Ethereum, BNB Chain and Base, and the project site publishes the same satUSD omni-CDP, Smart Vault and Prime Vault product set, so the BNB Chain representation Kraken lists is the one the project publishes. satUSD is a separate asset and no native-gas-coin claim is made.

Kraken publishes the asset as Storj on Ethereum (ERC-20) and its asset page states that nodes are paid in "the Ethereum-based ERC20 STORJ token". Independently, Storj's own node documentation on storj.dev publishes the exact token contract -- "the STORJ Token smart contract address 0xB64ef51C888972c908CFacf59B47C1AfBC0Ab8aC" -- and a second official FAQ page titled "ERC20-compatible wallet address for STORJ tokens" binds the same ticker to an Ethereum ERC-20 payout asset of the Storj network. Kraken lists the ERC-20 token and the record makes no native-coin claim.

scope: Source-coverage universe identity only: not investability, not capacity, not venue selection, not candidate promotion, not Regime activation, not Production wiring, not trading authority.
verification_bar: Two independent official sources per asset: the retained Kraken catalog (enabled asset with exactly one online <ASSET>/USD pair) plus Kraken's published asset name and network, matched independently against a project/foundation protocol document, token contract publication, migration notice or exact-contract asset report. Ticker text alone was not accepted. Kraken's own metadata carries no chain, contract or genesis field, so Kraken alone never satisfies the bar. Where the project publishes an exact contract or mint (STORJ, MET, RIVER, GALA) the record binds that identifier; where it publishes only the chain and token standard (DENT) the record says so explicitly and claims no contract. Where two independent official sources could not be obtained, no record would have been written at all.
